children: The partnership will develop green energy projects and explore opportunities across renewable power, adding momentum to India’s expanding clean-energy investment pipeline

PTC India and NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL) have formed a joint venture to develop green energy projects and pursue opportunities across India’s renewable power market, as energy companies accelerate investments in clean generation and related infrastructure. The new entity, NIRL PTC Renewables Limited, was incorporated on September 16, 2026, with NIRL holding a 74 per cent stake and PTC India owning the remaining 26 per cent. The incorporation followed approval from the Department of Investment and Public Asset Management under the Ministry of Finance. The joint venture builds on an agreement between the two companies to explore renewable energy projects with potential capacity of up to 2,000 MW. The proposed portfolio includes solar, wind, hydro, battery energy storage systems and other emerging green technologies.

India’s renewable energy market is witnessing sustained capacity additions as developers, utilities and power-sector companies seek to align portfolios with rising electricity demand and the country’s clean-energy targets.

According to the Ministry of New and Renewable Energy, India had 295.55 GW of installed renewable energy capacity as of August 31, 2026. Solar capacity stood at 168.04 GW, while wind capacity reached 58.52 GW. The country added 20.87 GW of renewable capacity during the first five months of FY27. The government has also set a target of achieving 500 GW of non-fossil fuel-based installed electricity capacity by 2030.

India crossed 300 GW of non-fossil capacity in July 2026, accounting for more than 60 per cent of the 2030 target. For PTC India and NIRL, the venture provides a structure to combine project development capabilities with power-market expertise. The partners had earlier outlined plans to develop renewable projects in phases and explore opportunities involving power sales to distribution companies, government entities and commercial and industrial consumers.

The expansion of renewable generation is also creating demand for storage, flexible power and integrated energy solutions. Battery storage and hybrid projects are increasingly being considered alongside solar and wind developments to improve grid reliability and manage variable renewable generation. Industry experts said such partnerships can help companies share project-development risks, mobilise capital and build larger renewable portfolios while responding to growing demand for reliable low-carbon electricity.

The latest venture also comes as NLC India expands its renewable-energy portfolio. Separately, NLC India has initiated the transfer of 708.96 MW of renewable energy assets, including a 4 MW green hydrogen project, to NLC India Renewables. The formation of the JV signals the growing role of strategic partnerships in India's transition towards a more diversified power mix, with renewable generation, storage and emerging green technologies becoming increasingly important to future energy investment.
